issue_context.title: Auto-correction breaks code by `Lint/ParenthesesAsGroupedExpression`
issue_context.body:
# Steps to reproduce the problem

I ran `rubocop -a --only Lint/ParenthesesAsGroupedExpression` on the following codes.

```ruby
a = [1, 2]
a.concat (1..2).map { |i| i * 10 }
p a
```

the fix breaks the code.

## Expected behavior

```ruby
a.concat (1..1).map { |i| i * 10 }   # Either leave it as it is,
a.concat((1..2).map { |i| i * 10 })  # or add extra parenthesis
```

## Actual behavior

```ruby
a.concat(1..2).map { |i| i * 10 } # It removes the space
```

```
$ rubocop --debug -a concat.rb
For ~/til: configuration from ~/til/.rubocop.yml
Default configuration from ~/.rbenv/versions/3.1.0/lib/ruby/gems/3.1.0/gems/rubocop-1.39.0/config/default.yml
```

## RuboCop version

```console
$ rubocop -V

```

review_comments: This cop is not aimed at the rule of adding parentheses. In other words, this case is a false positive and it should be `expect_no_offenses`, not `expect_offense`.
Please add a test case for Ruby 2.7's numbered parameter as well.

In this case, the block argument is in parentheses, so there are no new parentheses to be added.
Therefore, this one should remain in offense. How about it?

> Please add a test case for Ruby 2.7's numbered parameter as well.

Indeed it is. I added test cases.
Ah, this case is correct using `expect_offense` 👍
